title: Alto saxophone
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS alto saxophone (maker and model unstated on the page)
summary: Stand-in saxophone, not a measured one. No tone holes: each note is the printed mouthpiece, neck and bell cones joined by one straight cone cut to that note's length, where a real saxophone plays these notes with holes. The reed's opening, width and area are borrowed. C4 is blown at mf, E3 and F3 at ff, because they are silent at mf on this reed. One mouthpiece position, pushed in 13.28 mm and solved once on C4's passive peak, leaves the three at +18.1, -16.9 and -14.5 c from equal temperament. All three are cleaner than the recordings, and C4 has a hole at its seventh harmonic. Ab4 and E5 have no render.
physics_present: The printed neck (ISMA 2007), bell and mouthpiece (Lefebvre 2010) joined by one straight body cone whose slope is set once from the lowest note, Db3, and cut to each note's length
An alto reed fitted to a Lefebvre mouthpiece (his printed mass per area, resonance and damping); its opening 1.7 mm, width 10 mm and area 7.5e-5 m2 are borrowed
One mouthpiece position for every note, pushed in 13.28 mm, solved once on C4's passive first peak against equal temperament
Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures for two alto players
Reed noise, the duct-constriction law (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990), extrapolated, with no level set against a recording
A flanged bell radiating into room air with ISO 9613 absorption, 0.5 m on axis, at 48 kHz because the engine refuses this bell at 96 kHz
physics_missing: Tone holes, pads, chimneys, key rise and a fingering chart: no measured alto air column is printed, so no hole lattice is built
A measured alto reed opening, width and area: the opening is an unplayed-tip upper bound, the width a tenor reed's and the area Lefebvre's illustrative value
The right pitch: one position cannot close a 35 c spread, since C4 was already 11.6 c above E3 and F3 before the push
The recordings' spectra and noise: harmonics-to-noise reads 5 to 7 dB above the recordings on all three notes, and C4's centroid is 804 Hz against 405 Hz
The second register: Ab4 and E5 need a register hole and are not rendered
